data.text/markdown:
A filtration on your own simplices with phlite

The Vietoris–Rips complex of ||(n||) points has ||(\binom{n}{3}||) triangles. In the plane the Delaunay triangulation has only about ||(2n||), and filtering it by edge length still finds the loops of a point cloud (this is close to the alpha complex). We build it with scipy, hand the simplices to phlite as tuples, and draw the representative loops on the points.

data.text/markdown:
The chain complex and its filtration

Simplices are tuples of vertices; their boundary is the usual alternating sum, which we give as a mapping from faces to coefficients (here over ||(\mathbb{Z}/3||), to show that coefficients other than ||(\pm 1||) work too). Edges get their length; vertices appear at 0, and triangles with their longest edge (extend=True).

Two H1 points stand far from the diagonal: the two circles. Here are the edges of the complex at a scale where both loops are present, with their representatives (lists of (edge, coefficient)) drawn on top.

Watching the filtration

At scale ||(s||) the complex has every edge of length at most ||(s||), and every triangle whose edges are all there. Components merge as edges appear; each circle closes into a loop, which is filled in once its triangles span the middle. On the right, the bars alive at ||(s||) are highlighted.
